parsed.explanation: Combined regime: national binary-sex document and entry rules, possible refusal and lifetime fraud finding, a national-legislature bathroom restriction operating in this seat despite no local ban, and documented severe immigration-custody abuse create traveller-facing exposure. No general criminalisation of trans identity and active courts/local low-risk placement mitigate, but local protections are overridable and facilities/custody harms are state-imposed. Minors face care and school-related restrictions. This is not execution-level but sits well below safe-tier.

entry_documents.exposure: National binary-sex order; new X passports stopped; entry cable directs refusal where documents/records conflict or sex is doubted, with possible lifetime fraud ineligibility. Foreign advisories followed detentions.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports remain valid until expiry; passport policy is under court challenge and some orders are enjoined. No visitor-specific waiver is documented.
entry_documents.interaction: Mismatch at visa or border can trigger secondary screening, refusal, or immigration detention; airline checks add exposure.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Immigration custody: trans men report forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and sexual abuse. National corrections use conversion-style policies, deny hormones, and stopped reporting trans prisoner numbers.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Court injunctions block some executive orders; a national hate-crime law exists. No documented effective safeguard for immigration detainees or birth-sex custody is shown.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Document discrepancy or fraud allegation can move a traveller into immigration custody, where placement and abuse risks are documented.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: National order bars gender-congruent access to government-funded single-sex facilities; a national-legislature bathroom restriction operates in this seat; December 2024 protesters were arrested. Visitor scope is unspecified.
federal_state_facilities.protection: The seat has no local bathroom ban and a July 2026 assessment lists it low-risk for targeting trans adults.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: National override means the local council cannot repeal the facility restriction; enforcement runs through national institutions.

care_services.exposure: Gender-affirming care for minors is banned in 27 states/provinces; national rules proposed to bar insurance coverage under 18; executive orders are hostile to gender-affirming care. Adult visitor care denial is not documented.
care_services.protection: Adult care is not nationally banned in the dossier; some health rules are proposed or enjoined. Court challenges are pending.
care_services.interaction: A travelling minor needing care may face refusal or record exposure; an adult's emergency-care exposure is undocumented.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Counterterrorism strategy lists 'radically pro-transgender' groups among violent targets; justice memo references 'radical gender ideology'; schools face investigation or prosecution over pronouns and social transition.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Strategy says counterterrorism will not target mere disagreement; courts have blocked some orders; national hate-crime statute covers gender identity.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Framing increases scrutiny of visible advocacy and gender-nonconforming minors, feeding border, school and custody exposure.

minors_guardians.exposure: Minors face care bans in many states, sports ban, school bathroom restrictions, and an executive order threatening teachers who use preferred names or pronouns; hospital records of under-19 patients were subpoenaed.
minors_guardians.protection: Some orders are enjoined; no national ban on adult care; local low-risk placement is not shown to protect minors from national rules.
minors_guardians.interaction: National rules override local protection; a parent seeking care for a trans minor may face provider refusal, investigation, or record disclosure.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No trans-specific violence rate or local police practice is documented. Public opinion shows majority support for birth-sex documents and sports restrictions. Absence of incidents is not evidence of safety.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime law covers gender identity; 22 states plus the capital ban gender-identity discrimination; local low-risk assessment. Local enforcement is undocumented.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Reporting and police response in this seat are unresolved; national hate-crime coverage may not ensure local recourse.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Entry-refusal and fraud findings have limited visitor remedy; the attached bathroom restriction is not locally repealable; local police, custody and scope of the ban are unsourced.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Active litigation has enjoined some orders; passport suit is pending; national hate-crime and employment protections exist; July 2026 low-risk listing.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Courts can block some national measures but cannot cure all border, facility or custody practices; local law is vulnerable to national override.

anchor_checks.comparison: Far higher than 0.15-A: no general criminalisation of gender presentation, no documented capital path, and courts function partially. But this case has real facility exclusion and severe immigration-custody abuse, so it is not near the 0.15 tier.

Similar to 0.35-A in administrative exclusion and humiliation, but here custody abuse and a criminal-trespass facility enforcement are documented, while entry exclusion is less universal; local low-risk placement offsets somewhat.
Below 0.55-B: both have border screening and refusal, but this dossier adds possible lifetime fraud, facility trespass arrest, and severe immigration-custody harm, which 0.55-B lacks.

Well below 0.75-C: no trained-border or reliable-remedy regime; instead national override, facility restriction, and documented custodial abuse. 0.75-C's brief detention with working remedies is far safer.

parsed.synthesis: The sharpest exposures are national and operate directly in the seat: document mismatch can produce refusal or a fraud finding; a national-legislature bathroom restriction applies despite no local ban; and immigration custody has documented beatings, forced labour, solitary confinement and sexual abuse. Local low-risk placement and court injunctions are genuine but partial mitigations, since national action can override local law and facility/custody practices are institutional. Minors face care and school-related restrictions. No execution pathway is documented, but the combination of universal facility exclusion, possible criminal trespass, and severe detention conditions keeps the rating in the high-risk band.
